figures.label: Figure 1
figures.legend: Study pipeline. RR intervals derived from ambulatory ECG beat annotations are cut into 60-beat windows and scored by a window-level AF detector. The patient-adaptive hidden Markov quantifier (PA-HMMQ) treats the patient's window sequence as a two-state Markov chain whose rhythm dynamics are re-estimated for each patient (maximum-a-posteriori expectation–maximisation with a prior centred on source dynamics from calibration patients A), and returns the posterior expected burden. Posterior sampling gives a model-based standard deviation that is converted into a 90% conformal interval using calibration patients B. External cohorts are never used for training or calibration.
figures.alt: Flow diagram with five boxes in a row: ambulatory ECG beat annotations to RR intervals, 60-beat windows, window detector producing AF probability, patient-adaptive HMM quantifier, and burden with 90% conformal interval. Three boxes below feed into the last three: calibration patients A, posterior sampling, calibration patients B.

figures.label: Figure 2
figures.legend: Per-patient AF-burden mean absolute error (percentage points) of all burden estimators in the development test set and three external cohorts, LightGBM detector. Points, mean over five seeds; bars, ±1 SD. Blue, PA-HMMQ variants: pre-registered (calibrated-histogram emissions), final (probability emissions, Amendment A1) and R1 (post-hoc per-detector emission selection). HMM-src (final emissions): fixed source dynamics with the final emissions. Abbreviations as in Table 2.
figures.alt: Four dot-plot panels, one per cohort, listing twelve burden estimators on the vertical axis and mean absolute error on the horizontal axis; in the external cohorts the final PA-HMMQ and the fixed-dynamics HMM with the same emissions have the lowest errors.

figures.label: Figure 3
figures.legend: Bland–Altman plots of estimated versus reference AF burden in the pooled external cohorts for classify-and-count (left) and the final PA-HMMQ (right), LightGBM detector, estimates averaged over seeds. Hollow markers: patients with any reference atrial flutter. Solid line, mean difference; dashed lines, 95% limits of agreement. The diagonal band of points with large positive differences consists mainly of Icentia11k patients labelled atrial flutter, whose irregular ventricular response is classified as AF.
figures.alt: Two scatter plots of difference against mean burden. Most points lie on zero; a diagonal line of hollow points with large positive differences corresponds to flutter patients; the right panel shows a slightly smaller bias.

figures.label: Figure 4
figures.legend: Empirical coverage (left; mean over seeds, bars minimum–maximum) and mean interval width (right, log scale; median over seeds, bars minimum–maximum) of 90% per-patient burden intervals by method and cohort, LightGBM detector. Dashed line, nominal coverage 0.90. Normalised: nonconformity scaled by the posterior standard deviation; constant-width: unscaled absolute residual; CrI, uncalibrated posterior credible interval.
figures.alt: Two dot-plot panels. Left: coverage of eight interval methods in four cohorts relative to a dashed 0.90 line; the posterior credible interval under-covers and SHDB-AF is below 0.90 for most methods. Right: mean interval width on a logarithmic axis, smallest for the normalised conformal intervals.

figures.label: Figure 5
figures.legend: Robustness of burden estimators in SHDB-AF to simulated missed and false R peaks (2%, 5%), R-peak timing jitter (SD 10 and 25 ms) and premature beats with compensatory pauses (5%, 10%), for the LightGBM (left) and RRNet (right) detectors. Mean absolute error ± SD over seeds.
figures.alt: Two line charts of mean absolute error across nine perturbation conditions for six estimators; errors rise most with 25-ms jitter and, for RRNet, with missed beats; the final PA-HMMQ has the lowest error in every condition.

figures.label: Figure 6
figures.legend: Mean absolute error by reference burden stratum in the pooled external cohorts (LightGBM detector; logarithmic axis). Strata: AF-free (0%), >0–1%, >1–10%, >10–50% and >50% burden. Lines connect strata for readability only.
figures.alt: Line chart with five burden strata on the horizontal axis and error on a logarithmic vertical axis for four estimators; errors are highest in the >0–1% stratum and above 10%; the calibrated-emission HMM is best above 50%.
